Constraints, phase, energy and rounding effects are reported separately. These additional validation supplements are managed separately from the common 22-example registry. SHAKE and RATTLE: constraints and momentum ownership Ten fixed pendulum evolutions distinguish position constraints, full-time tangent momentum and interior centered momentum. Methods, equations, figures and references Assumptions, units and boundaries L=m=g=1, initial angle 0.7 and zero angular velocity. C=(q·q−1)/2, T=100 and h=0.04/0.02/0.01; position targets are fixed at 1e−13, with a coarse 1e−10 companion. Editorial clarification Original SHAKE and RATTLE full texts remain unread; selected author lecture notes were inspected. The finite-difference symplectic defect is a local proxy, not a general proof, and centered SHAKE velocity is not assigned RATTLE tangency. Axes for trajectories, states, time or iterations do not represent physical spatial dimensions. Adopted numerical method Original scalar Newton position constraints, RATTLE final tangent impulses and SHAKE position pairs. SHAKE momentum is centered only at interior nodes; endpoint momenta are absent. SHAKE solves columns are eta, eta/h^2, position residual and Newton updates. Column1 uses the uniform recurrence normalization eta/h^2. For the first constrained half-step startup, the physical multiplier is 2*eta/h^2; later full position-Verlet steps use eta/h^2. Reverse-pair steps all use the later recurrence convention. RATTLE has its separate five-column normalization. No scientific gate or plot uses SHAKE column1.
